title: Getting Started with Anvi'o
author: Murat Eren and Bonnie Hurwitz
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.gc3bsyn

steps.title: Download and prepare contigs file
steps.instruction: Download the fixed contigs FASTA file from the HPC and save it as contigs.fa in the anvi'o directory.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the FASTA file has simple deflines; fix them prior to mapping if necessary.
Execute the download command: scp netid@sftp.hpc.arizona.edu:/rsgrps/bh_class/username/assembly/megahit-out/fixed-contigs.fa contigs.fa

steps.title: Create the initial contigs database
steps.instruction: Generate the contigs.db file from contigs.fa using the anvi-gen-contigs-database command.

substeps.instruction: Run the command: anvi-gen-contigs-database -f contigs.fa -o contigs.db

Note: The process computes k-mer frequencies (default size 4, adjustable via --kmer-size), soft-splits contigs longer than 20,000 kbp (adjustable via --split-length), and identifies ORFs using Prodigal.
Optional: Use --skip-mindful-splitting to skip splitting for very large assemblies, --skip-gene-calling to skip gene calling, or --external-gene-calls to provide custom gene calls.

steps.title: Decorate database with HMM hits
steps.instruction: Run the HMM profiling command to identify hits from bacterial single-copy core gene collections using HMMER.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Use --hmm-profile-dir to specify a custom HMM profile directory.
Optional: Use --num-threads to utilize multiple CPUs and improve runtime.
